arquivo.titulo: General patterns and predictors of thermal tolerance in bees: A global synthesis across taxa and environments
arquivo.autores: Fernanda Baena‐Díaz, Misael Morales-Gómez, Brenda Ratoni, Victor Hugo Gonzalez, Wesley Dáttilo
arquivo.resumo: Understanding how organisms respond to temperature variation has become central to ecology and evolution because of its role in shaping species’ physiology, distribution, and ecological interactions. Thermal tolerances are critical for ectothermic organisms, which have evolved a variety of behavioral and physiological strategies to manage thermal stress that vary widely across geographic and temporal scales. This study synthesizes existing information on bees’ critical thermal maximum (CT Max ) and minimum (CT Min ) through a systematic review of published data. Despite bees’ ecological…

arquivo.titulo: Gut microbiome and host metabolome dynamics in pre-diapause bumble bee future queens
arquivo.autores: Logan Sauers, Jilian Li, Liuhao Wang, Zhihao Zhang, Yulong Guo, Mingsheng Zhuang et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract    Microbiomes vary over time in response to host physiology, inter-microbial interactions, and host-microbiome feedback. Changes in life stage alter host behavior and physiology, exerting strong filters on their microbiomes. Bumble bee queens undergo a critical life stage transition from residing in parental colonies to mating and solitary diapause. Previous work highlights declines in core microbes during this transition, but directionality between the changing microbiome and host physiology remains unclear. To test the temporal relationship between the microbiome and host…

arquivo.titulo: Heat tolerance in bees: a meta-analysis of ecological, evolutionary, and methodological drivers
arquivo.autores: Suntaree Karnchananiyom, Natapot Warrit, Patrice Pottier, Kanuengnit Wayo, Carmen Silva, Vanessa Kellermann et al.
arquivo.resumo: Climate change poses a growing threat to bees, which provide essential pollination services in natural and agricultural ecosystems. Although the critical thermal maximum (CTmax) is widely used to assess the vulnerability of pollinators to climate change, we lack a comprehensive understanding of the factors shaping heat tolerance across bee species globally. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of experimental CTmax measurements, extracting 339 effect sizes from 35 studies spanning 198 bee species. arquivo.titulo: Climate Change, Pollinator Displacement and Human–Bee Conflict: A One Health Framework for Emerging Ecological and Public Health Risks
arquivo.autores: Amit Kumar Awasthi
arquivo.resumo: Reports of mass honey-bee stinging incidents in and around Unnao district, Uttar Pradesh — including a fatal attack during a local cricket match in February 2026 — have renewed attention to a poorly studied interface: the conditions under which honey-bee colonies and human populations come into damaging contact. This paper develops a One Health framework for interpreting such events across three interacting domains — environmental/ecosystem health, pollinator (Apis dorsata) health and behaviour, and human public health — rather than treating each incident as an isolated news item. arquivo.titulo: Transcriptomic Insights into the Molecular Response of Stingless Bees (Tetragonula pagdeni) to Low-Temperature Stress
arquivo.autores: Xinmeng Li, Yuzhu Huo, Dahe Yang, Changsheng Ma, Hua Wang, Tianzheng Xu et al.

arquivo.titulo: Bee Pollinators Enhance B-onion Seed Production in the Dry Zone of Sri Lanka
arquivo.autores: Herath A, Karunaratne I
arquivo.resumo: Production of B-onion (Allium cepa), a key cash crop in Sri Lanka, falls short of consumer demand due to limited quality seeds and high cost of commercial seeds. arquivo.autores: Ciaran Harris, Francis L. W. Ratnieks, Nicholas J. Balfour
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Foraging bees often work within fine energetic margins, but recent work has shown that foraging conditions can vary markedly across the year. Despite the importance of seasonality for pollinator foraging, most work in this area has relied on indirect approaches. arquivo.autores: Shujuan Xu, Ruirui Liu, Qingxia Zhang, Wenfan Zeng, Shengrui Liang, Guobin Lan et al.
arquivo.resumo: Pollination services provided by insects are fundamental to the productivity and quality of sweet cherry orchards. This study investigated the flower-visiting insect community and compared the pollination potential of A. mellifera and A. cerana in a sweet cherry orchard on the Loess Plateau of eastern Gansu, China. Thus, it is critical to identify additional resources for pollinators. arquivo.autores: Majid Ikram, Madapuji Rajagopalan Srinivasan, A. Suganthi, Vangili Ramasami Saminathan, J. Auxcilia, Jayakanthan Mannu et al.
arquivo.resumo: Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus (Thunb.) Matsum. & Nakai) is a highly pollinator-dependent crop in which honey bees play a vital role in ensuring successful fruit set and yield. arquivo.resumo: Wildfires are a natural disturbance in dry ponderosa pine forest ecosystems, and are increasing in frequency and severity across western North America. The effects of wildfire on biotic and abiotic conditions have important implications for higher trophic levels, including native bees. arquivo.autores: Zeus Mateos‐Fierro, Ashley Leach, Doriana Mierow, John Ternest, Ian Kaplan

arquivo.autores: Jiaqi Li, Wenmi Wang, Yuanyuan Du, JUNXIA JIA, Zhaoming Wei

arquivo.resumo: Trigonisca townsendi is a tiny stingless bee from the dry forests of northwestern Peru, where it plays a role in pollination and the traditional medicinal use of honey. arquivo.titulo: A national checklist for monitoring Portugal’s pollinators (Anthophila, Syrphidae and Papilionoidea) under the EU Nature Restoration Regulation
arquivo.autores: Eduardo Marabuto, Francisco Gil, Hugo Gaspar, Albano Soares, Alperen Yayla, Ana Afonso et al.
arquivo.resumo: 1. Wild pollinators are declining across Europe, prompting new policy commitments. The EU Nature Restoration Regulation requires Member States to reverse pollinator decline and to monitor pollinator abundance and species richness. Effective implementation depends on robust national taxonomic baselines that define which species are present, where they occur and how they can be monitored consistently. 2. We present a policy-oriented national checklist for insect pollinators in the Portuguese territory, covering the three focal groups of the European Pollinator Monitoring Scheme: bees…

arquivo.titulo: New state records, annotated checklist, and distribution of Lasioglossum Curtis bees in Idaho (Hymenoptera: Halictidae)
arquivo.autores: Luc Leblanc, Joel Gardner, Karlee Davis, Stuart Murray, Anna Hawse, Nash Muckey
arquivo.resumo: An annotated checklist of the 62 species of Lasioglossum Curtis (Hymenoptera: Halictidae) bees present in the state of Idaho is provided, including 35 new state records. The checklist is based on label data from 5,252 preserved museum specimens and 75 additional records from published literature. A detailed distribution map and a phenology graph are provided for each species, in addition to floral association records based on field survey data and museum specimen label data.

arquivo.titulo: A survey of bees (Hymenoptera, Apoidea) in the Bear River Mountains in northern Utah
arquivo.autores: Lindsie M. McCabe, Byron Love, Jonathan Berenguer Uhuad Koch, Skyler J. Burrows, Kelsey K. Graham, Diana Cox-Foster
arquivo.resumo: Bees provide critical pollination services to a diversity of flowering plants, facilitating the function of terrestrial ecosystems and global food production. Here, we present a checklist of bee species collected in conjunction with a larger systematic study in the Bear River Mountains of northern Utah, United States, over the course of three consecutive summers (2020-2022). The survey was conducted on public lands managed by the United States Forest Service. We collected 8,500 bee specimens using pan traps, hand nets and trap nests, representing at least 199 bee species belonging to 33…

arquivo.titulo: Key to long horn bee species of the tribe Eucerini (Hymenoptera, Apoidea, Apidae) occurring in Europe
arquivo.autores: ACHIK DORCHIN, Blandine Rigaut, Denis Michez
arquivo.resumo: Europe hosts some 2180 wild bee species, representing ca 10% of the world bee diversity. The long horn bee tribe Eucerini (Hymenoptera, Apidae) is one of the most charismatic groups in this region, and is particularly diverse in the southern, Euro-Mediterranean region. While identification of most species is difficult, a comprehensive identification tool has largely been missing, but is essential for current monitoring programs. This work presents the first modern comprehensive key to species of the tribe Eucerini in Europe. Keys are provided separately for females and males, including 89 out…

arquivo.titulo: The Missing Branches of the Bee Tree of Life: Addressing Global Darwinian Shortfalls and Their Drivers
arquivo.autores: Felipe Walter Pereira, Matheus Lima Araujo, Anderson Lepeco, Bruno Ferreira Marques, Hugo Bampi, Lucas Jardim et al.
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Aim Estimate the Darwinian shortfall (i.e., the lack of knowledge about phylogenetic relationships) of bees worldwide, as well as identify their drivers. Location Global. Taxon Bees (Hymenoptera, Anthophila). Methods We built phylogenies for over 12,000 bee species, combining the most comprehensive phylogeny and an algorithm with random solutions to insert missing lineages. The Darwinian shortfall was quantified as the Phylogenetic Diversity (PD) deficit, the ratio of inserted branch lengths at the assemblage level. We identified potential ecological and socioeconomic drivers of the…

arquivo.titulo: Sociality and nesting strategy account for non-random associations between bees and their parasitic dipterans
arquivo.autores: Carlo Polidori, Andrea Ferrari
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Bees (Apoidea: Anthophila) are recorded as common hosts of a diverse array of parasitic Diptera species, but information is widely scattered across the literature, limiting our knowledge of global bee-dipteran association patterns. Here, we retrieved published information on 453 bee-dipteran associations to test the role of life-history traits of hosts and parasites on such patterns. The 13 families and 37 genera of Diptera associated with bees are unevenly distributed across bee families within a specialized and modular network. The family Apidae was the most associated with…

arquivo.titulo: Molecular detection and partial phylogenetic analysis of Deformed Wing Virus and Acute Bee Paralysis Virus in Varroa destructor samples
arquivo.autores: Ali Küçük, Yakup Yıldırım, Özge Sevinç Korkmaz Akar, Abdurrahman Anıl Çağırgan, Ayşegül Usta
arquivo.resumo: Varroa destructor is a significant mite that adversely affects honey bee health, both directly and as a vector for various pathogens. This study aimed to detect Deformed Wing Virus (DWV) and Acute Bee Paralysis Virus (ABPV) by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and to perform sequence and phylogenetic analyses of field isolates obtained from V. destructor samples collected in Burdur, Southwestern Türkiye. Mites were collected from five research regions (Karaçal, Kumluca, Akyaka, Yazıköy, and Çendik), with one apiary selected per region; colonies within each apiary were…

arquivo.titulo: Illustrated catalogue of type specimens of bees (Hymenoptera: Apoidea) housed in the Laboratorio de Abejas and Instituto de Ciencias Naturales de la Universidad Nacional de Colombia (LABUN and ICN)
arquivo.autores: NICOLÁS D. GUTIÉRREZ-RUBIANO, Fernando Fernández, Rodulfo Ospina, Diego A. Guevara
arquivo.resumo: Type specimens are the primary reference for species-level taxonomy and play a critical role in ensuring nomenclatural stability. However, in the Neotropics, access to these primary taxonomic resources remains limited, hindering species recognition and the resolution of nomenclatural issues. In Colombia, most bee type specimens are concentrated in two major collections at the Universidad Nacional de Colombia: the Laboratorio de Abejas (LABUN) and the National Insect Collection (CNI) of the Instituto de Ciencias Naturales (ICN). Here we present an illustrated catalogue of the bee type material…

arquivo.titulo: Hidden Amazonian diversity: integrative taxonomy reshapes the Melipona seminigra species complex (Hymenoptera: Apidae: Meliponini)
arquivo.autores: José Augusto dos Santos-Silva, David Silva Nogueira, Izaura Bezerra Francini, Júlio César Carvalho de Oliveira, Rogério Marcos de Oliveira Alves, Gislene Almeida Carvalho-Zilse et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Melipona seminigra is a polytypic complex of stingless bees broadly distributed throughout the Brazilian Amazon and of major ecological and economic importance due to its role in pollination and meliponiculture. Despite the considerable amount of taxonomic information accumulated over time, the identity and boundaries of its constituent forms have remained uncertain. In this study, we conducted an integrative taxonomic assessment based on specimens deposited in three institutional collections, combining traditional morphological analyses with molecular species-delimitation approaches…

arquivo.titulo: A Catalogue of the Bee (Hymenoptera: Apoidea) Flora in Campeche, Mexico
arquivo.autores: Maximiliano Vanoye Eligio, Benito Bernardo Dzib Castillo, Edith González Lazo, Félix Alejandra Luna Medina, Blanca Del Rosario Martín Canché, Juan Manuel Ortega Almeyda et al.
arquivo.resumo: Beekeeping is an activity that generates significant income in various parts of the world. Beekeeping success and production depend largely on the native and exotic flora that surrounds apiaries. The flora influences bee success as well as the nutritional and organoleptic characteristics of honey, so its knowledge is essential for the development and growth of this activity. Therefore, herein we present an updated catalogue listing the flora important to the success of beekeeping in the state of Campeche, Mexico. We reviewed publications available in scientific databases related to the…

arquivo.titulo: Metagenomics reveals biogeography and functional potential of phage communities in bee gut
arquivo.autores: Zhengyi Zhang, Fan Yang, Zhihao Zhang, Fugang Liu, Mingsheng Zhuang, Jilian Li
arquivo.resumo: Bacteriophages (phages) are pivotal regulators of microbiome ecology and function, yet their distribution, diversity and ecological roles within the bee gut remain largely unexplored, particularly across diverse bee species and geographic regions. Here, we used a large-scale metagenomic dataset to investigate phage communities associated with seven bee species across China. We recovered 121 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) from 132 bee gut metagenomes, revealing that bee gut phages are dominated by the class Caudoviricetes and include numerous previously uncharacterized viral…

arquivo.titulo: Diversity of Mites Associated With Stingless Bees (Hymenoptera: Meliponini) in Forest Fragments in Brazil: Empirical Validation of an Efficient and Low‐Cost Sampling Method
arquivo.autores: Éricles Charles da Silva Melo, Milena Emily da Silva Lima, Vinícius Borges da Silva, Airton Torres Carvalho, Simão Dias Vasconcelos
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Despite the importance of understanding mite–bee interactions, standardized and noninvasive methods for sampling mite communities in stingless bee hives remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate a novel, low‐cost sampling technique using a custom‐built suction device, the Portable Mite Aspirator (PMA), for collecting mites from hives of three stingless bee species that were evaluated as healthy: Melipona scutellaris , Melipona subnitida and Scaptotrigona depilis . The research was conducted across two ecosystems, tropical rainforest and dry forest, in northeastern Brazil. The PMA…

arquivo.titulo: New records of wild bees (Hymenoptera, Apoidea) from Galicia, northwestern Spain
arquivo.autores: Alejandro Núñez, Piluca Álvarez Fidalgo, Inés Jiménez Fernández, Carlos Fernández Álvarez, Álvaro Asenjo Guerra, Yamil Jiménez Rodríguez et al.
arquivo.revista: Boletín de la Asociación Española de Entomología/Boletín de la Asociación Española de Entomología/Suplementos del Boletín de la Asociación Española de Entomología
arquivo.resumo: Galicia (northwestern Spain) has historically received limited survey effort for wild bees, resulting in a significant gap in faunistic knowledge compared with other Iberian regions. Within the framework of the national project Polinizadores: mejora de conocimiento, standardized surveys were conducted in eight 1 × 1 km plots distributed across the four Galician provinces during two consecutive campaigns (2023 and 2024). In 2023, bees were sampled using pan traps, whereas in 2024 specimens were collected by active netting along standardized transects. All collected material was identified by…

arquivo.titulo: Biogeographic and Habitat-Associated Variation in the Gut Microbiota of the Stingless Bee Tetragonula laeviceps Between Bali and Lombok, Two Islands Situated on Opposite Sides of the Wallace Line
arquivo.autores: Joko Pilianto, Amr S. Abou El‐Ela, J Li, Du Tianxiang, Mochammad Syamsul Hadi, Asim Munawar et al.
arquivo.resumo: Biogeographic barriers are well known to structure animal and plant diversity, but whether they are associated with variation in host-associated microbiomes, especially in tropical pollinators, remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated gut bacterial community variation in the stingless bee Tetragonula laeviceps (Apidae: Meliponini) collected from Bali and Lombok, two Indonesian islands situated on opposite sides of the Wallace Line. Using 16S rRNA gene V3–V4 amplicon sequencing, we analyzed 12 colony-level samples collected from forest and agroforestry habitats on both islands.…

arquivo.titulo: Toxicogenomic and structural determinants of cytochrome P450-mediated insecticide detoxification and selectivity in bee pollinators
arquivo.autores: Xingzhi Xiao
arquivo.resumo: Bee pollinators provide essential ecosystem services but face multiple threats, including exposure to insecticides. Current pesticide risk assessments rely on empirical toxicity testing of a limited number of bee species (primarily Apis mellifera), which inadequately predict sensitivity across more than 20,000 bee species globally. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying differential pesticide sensitivity in bees is essential for effective pollinator protection. Cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (P450s), particularly the CYP9Q subfamily in honey bees (A. mellifera), have emerged as key…

arquivo.titulo: From pollen to patterns: authentication and geographical classification of stingless bee honey by melissopalynology and chemometrics
arquivo.autores: Hector Hernán Hernández Zarta, Sebastián J. Caruso, Jéssica B. Ressutte, Cynthia Fernandes Pinto da Luz, Ofélia Anjos, Wilma Aparecida Spinosa et al.

arquivo.titulo: Thrinchostoma Saussure, little known bee genus from China, with description of a new species (Hymenoptera: Halictidae)
arquivo.autores: Ze‐Qing Niu, Yuan Feng, Pia Oremek, Feng Liu, Chao‐Dong Zhu
arquivo.revista: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
arquivo.resumo: Zeqing Niu, Feng Yuan, Pia Oremek, Feng Liu, Chaodong Zhu (2016): Thrinchostoma Saussure, little known bee genus from China, with description of a new species (Hymenoptera: Halictidae). Zoological Systematics 41 (2): 207-215, DOI: 10.11865/zs.201619

arquivo.titulo: Toward Quality Standards for Brazilian Native Stingless Bee Honey Based on Physicochemical and Antioxidant Analyses
arquivo.autores: María Cristina Marcucci, Thais Bonagura, Thamires Bonagura, Geovani Moreira da Cruz, Carolina Passarelli Gonçalves, Yuyang Guo et al.
arquivo.resumo: Samples of stingless honey from six species of stingless bees collected at nine stations in different Brazilian states were analyzed by chemometric methods for moisture, impurities and solid residues, ash, pH, electrical conductivity, proteins, proline, identification of adulteration, presence of substances such as phytochemical analysis, color and levels of HMF. The color (C) varied between water white and dark amber. Proteins (mL) varied from 0.00 (S5) to 2.00 (S4). Lund test from 0.00% (S5) to 3.10% (S6), total phenols (TP%) from 0.04 to 13.45 mg/100 g GAE, total flavonoids from (TF%) 0.03…

arquivo.titulo: MSA: A Persuasion-Grounded Taxonomy of Elder-Fraud Mechanisms, Signals, and Archetypes
arquivo.autores: Ravi Sundaar, Pamela B. Teaster
arquivo.revista: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
arquivo.resumo: Elder-fraud defense has no shared vocabulary. Regulators count scam categories. Law enforcement counts crime types. Industry groups count phishing campaigns. Gerontology explains how persuasion works. These descriptions have been connected before, most systematically by Beals and colleagues, but none is designed to drive detection while an encounter is still running. Cyber defense had the same problem until MITRE ATT&CK gave defenders a common language for attacker behavior. This paper introduces MSA (Mechanism, Signal and Archetype), a three-level taxonomy of elder fraud. A Mechanism is the…

arquivo.titulo: Mitochondrial Genome Assemblies of Four “Bee-Assassin” (Hemiptera: Reduviidae: Apiomerus) Recovered Using Shallow Whole-Genome sequencing
arquivo.autores: Andrés M. Gómez-Palacio, Sandra Uribe-Soto, Carolina Ortiz-Muñoz, Dimitri Forero
arquivo.resumo: Apiomerus (“bee-assassin” assassin bugs) is a Neotropical genus of Reduviidae with ecological importance as a group of predatory insects and notable morphological diversity, yet mitochondrial genomic resources have remained unavailable for the genus. We generated low-coverage whole-genome sequencing data from four vouchered specimens collected in Colombia and reconstructed mitochondrial genomes for Apiomerus sp., A. ochropterus , A. luctuosus , and A. nitidicollis . Quality-filtered reads were assembled using an organelle-specific GetOrganelle workflow, and the resulting assembly graphs and…

arquivo.titulo: Under-sampled KBAs, over-sampled roadsides: integrating historical and contemporary records of Malagasy bees
arquivo.autores: Damselle Quesada, Nicolas Leclercq, Leon Marshall, Ciaran E.D. Clark, Aina N. Razakamiaramanana, Nicolas J. Vereecken
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Madagascar hosts exceptional biodiversity and endemism, yet its native bee fauna remains poorly characterised. We assembled and cleaned the first comprehensive occurrence dataset for Malagasy bees, reducing 10,721 raw records to 4,071 validated occurrences covering 218 georeferenced species of the 224 checklist species across six families (89.3% endemic). Despite near-complete checklist coverage, the dataset remains critically sparse for Madagascar’s size, with most species documented by only a few records. Sampling was highly uneven across taxa: most genera were underrepresented…

arquivo.titulo: Guarani stingless-bee ethnospecies, traditional management, and perceived threats: a systematic scoping review from the Atlantic Forest
arquivo.autores: Walkiria Aparecida Benites, Laura Jane Gisloti
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Stingless bees (Meliponini) are important Neotropical pollinators but remain underrepresented in Brazilian conservation policy. We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-guided systematic scoping review of published and grey literature on Guarani Mbya and Kaiowá stingless-bee ethnospecies, perceived threats, and traditional management in the Atlantic Forest and associated agrofrontiers. Five studies published between 2005 and 2021 met the inclusion criteria; a multilingual update in July 2026 identified no additional eligible study. We recorded 24 hymenopteran ethnospecies entries, including 22…

arquivo.titulo: ABCGSA: A Novel Hybrid Artificial Bee Colony Gravitational Search Algorithm for Feature Selection of Fingerprint Intramodal Biometric System
arquivo.autores: Janet Olubunmi Jooda, Sunday A. Ajagbe, Misan Paul Etchie, Oluyinka Titilayo Adedeji, Alice O. Oke, Pragasen Mudali
arquivo.resumo: The feature selection (FS) algorithm extracts the most relevant and significant data from the large-dimensional feature space in the dataset, enhancing the biometric system’s classification accuracy. However, optimizing the feature diversity of high-dimensional feature space of the FS algorithm has been given little attention in existing FS algorithms. Therefore, a hybrid artificial bee colony (ABC)- based disruptive selection and Gravitational Search Algorithm (GSA) to form ABCGSA for enhanced FS prior to the classification phase of Fingerprint Intramodal Biometric System (FIBS) was…

arquivo.titulo: Floral adaptation and modular trait evolution associated with a shift from bee to hummingbird pollination
arquivo.autores: Pedro Juárez, Kathleen M. Kay
arquivo.resumo: Pollination shifts result in floral divergence, yet how such shifts influence variation and correlation among floral traits is unclear. We examine whether a transition from bee to hummingbird pollination in sister species of Neotropical spiral gingers - Costus kuntzei, with ancestral bee pollination, and Costus wilsonii, with derived hummingbird pollination - drives phenotypic variation, functional integration and morphological modularity. Using field measurements and observations, we assess pollinator assemblages and pollination syndrome divergence by quantifying a suite of floral traits…

arquivo.titulo: Deforestation Increases Developmental Instability in the Orchid Bee Euglossa imperialis Across Protected Areas of Panama
arquivo.autores: Fernando Moya, Tamara Segovia-Jara, Valeria Tapia, Catalina Aguilar, Jordan Hernandez-Martelo, Laura Milena Pérez et al.
arquivo.resumo: Habitat loss and deforestation are among the main drivers of biodiversity decline in tropical ecosystems, yet their effects on developmental stability remain poorly understood in many insect groups. Orchid bees (Apidae: Euglossini) have been proposed as potential bioindicators of environmental quality due to their close association with forested habitats and sensitivity to habitat disturbance. Here, we evaluated the relationship between forest cover, wing morphology, and developmental stability in the orchid bee Euglossa imperialis across five protected areas of Panama exhibiting different…

arquivo.titulo: First Report of Bacterial Dieback of Rice Caused by Pantoea anthophila in Guangxi, China
arquivo.autores: Zhiheng Zhang, Jingjue Wang, Dongkang Han, Tong Qin, Siyu Chen, Ruyi Wang et al.
arquivo.resumo: Rice is a major staple crop in China and worldwide, and bacterial diseases threaten its production (Doni et al. 2021; Lv et al. 2022). In 2025, typical leaf tip dieback symptoms were observed on rice seedlings in a rice field planted with cv. Fuxiangnian in Binyang County (23.25834°N, 108.92461°E), Guangxi, China. Symptoms initially appeared as reddish-brown blighted lesions at the leaf tips, gradually extending downward and eventually leading to complete leaf dieback. In severe cases, lesions coalesced and formed irregular necrotic areas. Approximately 667 ha were affected, and disease…

arquivo.titulo: Occurrence of Pantoea anthophila Causing Rhizome Rot Disease of Banana in China
arquivo.autores: Shangbo Jiang, Jin Zhang, Chanjuan Du, Di Yang, Yunfeng Ye, Lian Fu Pan et al.
arquivo.resumo: Banana (genus Musa) is an economically important fruit crop. In January 2026, a rhizome rot disease was observed in a banana plantation in Nanning, Guangxi, China, affecting more than 10% of cultivated plants. Infected plants initially showed no obvious aboveground symptoms; however, yellow to brown water-soaked spots appeared on the rhizomes. In severe cases, plants exhibited stunting and leaf yellowing. The decay was confined to the rhizome and did not have a foul odor. To isolate the pathogen, diseased tissues (5 × 5 mm) were dissected and surface-sterilized with 75% ethanol (30 s)…

arquivo.titulo: Vicariance and dispersal shape the colonization history of the Galápagos carpenter bee, Xylocopa darwini
arquivo.autores: Graham C McLaughlin, Verónica Baquero-Méndez, María José Pozo, María de Lourdes Torres, Brian Hollis
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Island colonization and subsequent diversification are often shaped by a complex interplay between organism-specific traits including dispersal capacity and ecological requirements, and the configuration of the landscape over geological time. Here, we investigate the evolutionary history and population genomics of the Galápagos carpenter bee, Xylocopa darwini , across six islands of the Galápagos archipelago. Despite the bees presumed strong flight ability, we find evidence of long-term isolation among all islands with the strongest divergence occurring between the eastern and…

arquivo.titulo: Spatial structure partially explains niche variation in urban Neotropical stingless bees
arquivo.autores: Raquel Bendocchi Alves, Vladimir Eliodoro Costa, Raul Costa‐Pereira
arquivo.resumo: Abstract The geographic distribution of consumers and their resources shapes the spatial signature of trophic interactions in heterogeneous landscapes. Bees are central place foragers that consume a wide variety of plant species around their nests, thus, bee communities in urban landscapes are an opportune system for understanding intra- and interspecific spatial variation in resource use. Here, we investigated how the spatial distribution of nests of four species of Neotropical stingless bees ( Tetragonisca angustula , Plebeia droryana , Nannotrigona testaceicornis , Scaptotrigona postica )…

arquivo.titulo: Optimization of High Molecular Weight DNA Extractions from Dried, Museum-Grade Insects Enables Long-Read Sequencing, Phylogenetics, and Methylation Profiling
arquivo.autores: Gabrielle A. Hartley, Richard J Green, Nicole Pauloski, Nicole M Tillquist, Phoebe Johnston, Sara Ord et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Developing an effective DNA extraction method that meets requirements for long-read sequencing of poorly preserved samples, such as museum specimens or ancient material, offers new opportunities for genomic analysis of endangered or extinct species for which samples are rare. However, these samples often yield degraded and highly fragmented DNA, rendering long-read sequencing infeasible for many specimens residing in museum collections. Herein, we demonstrate a protocol for successfully extracting DNA of sufficient quality for sequencing on the Oxford Nanopore Technologies long-read…

arquivo.titulo: Genomics Reveal Population Crash and Range Contraction in Elusive Fijian Hylaeus Bees
arquivo.autores: Tegan A. Edwards, Damien Esquerré, Nikolas P. Johnston, Stephen D. Galvin, Nikkita L. Maxwell, Francisco Encinas‐Viso et al.
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT The conservation of pollinators is of particular interest due to their keystone role in ecosystem function, but is hindered by systematic geographic and methodological biases such that baseline data are not often readily available. Islands are useful as simplified systems to understand evolutionary processes, are known to host higher bee species richness per unit area than mainland regions, and have disproportionate representation of threatened species. We used low‐lying and canopy sampling paired with mitochondrial and genomic data to assess a recently discovered clade of…

arquivo.titulo: Orchid bees (Hymenoptera: Apidae) in urban forest fragments of the provinces of Panama and Colón, Panama: an approach to their diversity
arquivo.autores: Janick Hernández, Carolina Chirú de Bracho, Vielka Murillo, Francisco Farnum, Ruben de la Guardia, Víctor Olivo et al.
arquivo.resumo: Orchid bees, or euglossines, are Neotropical pollinators which, in addition to preferentially inhabiting humid forests, also inhabit urban forest remnants within an anthropogenic matrix. However, the extent to which these fragments sustain diverse euglossine assemblages and how their community structure varies among urban remnants remain poorly understood. We therefore evaluated the diversity, evenness, dominance, and species composition of Euglossini in three urban forest fragments in Panama and Colón provinces, considering these remnants as habitat islands within a highly modified…

arquivo.titulo: Local and landscape drivers of taxonomic, functional, and compositional diversity of wild bees in urban and rural parks in Central Europe
arquivo.autores: Anna Sobieraj‐Betlińska, Piotr Szefer
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Wild bees contribute substantially to biodiversity in agricultural and urban landscapes, yet the relative importance of local habitat conditions, landscape context, and seasonal dynamics in shaping their communities remains insufficiently understood. Here, we studied wild bee communities, excluding managed honey bees, in 22 urban and rural parks in Central Europe. A total of 5763 individuals representing 188 species were recorded. We evaluated bee abundance, species richness, Shannon diversity, functional dispersion, and beta-diversity components in relation to local habitat…

arquivo.titulo: Pharmacological Mechanisms of Bee Venom Acupuncture : A Preclinical Systematic Review
arquivo.autores: Jaehwan Cho, Yejin hong, Dongwoo Nam
arquivo.resumo: This systematic review aims to investigate the pharmacological effects and causally supported mechanisms of bee venom acupuncture/pharmacopuncture and compositionally comparable whole bee venom interventions, including live bee sting interventions where applicable, based on preclinical in vivo, in vitro, and ex vivo studies. The review will systematically identify and synthesize evidence on pharmacological effects and the molecular, cellular, biochemical, and signaling mechanisms whose causal involvement has been experimentally evaluated.

arquivo.titulo: GRA Method for Bearing Fault Classification: Two-Stage Model with Statistical Feature Extraction
arquivo.autores: Vidhya
arquivo.revista: REST Journal on Advances in Mechanical Engineering
arquivo.resumo: The origins of literature and its study within the English tradition have been widely debated, particularly regarding its canons and contexts. Literature is no longer seen as a fixed, definable category but rather a socially constructed concept, shaped by historical and cultural factors. This paper examines the evolving nature of literature, particularly in relation to language and grammar changes in medieval English texts. The research discussed in these papers highlights key linguistic developments in medieval English, offering new perspectives on grammar, syntax, and literary analysis. By…

arquivo.titulo: Bee Venom-Loaded Nanoliposomes as an Antioxidant and Erythroprotective Delivery Platform for In Vitro Controlled Release and Improved Gastrointestinal Stability
arquivo.autores: Perla de Jesús Balcázar-Vega, Fridha Viridiana Villalpando Vargas, Paola Viridiana Martínez-Beltrán, Silvia Josefina López‐Pérez, Abril Ivett Priscilla Gómez-Guzman, Alioth Guerrero‐Aranda et al.
arquivo.resumo: Bee venom (BV) contains bioactive peptides with potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties, yet its direct therapeutic use is limited by cytotoxicity, instability, and uncontrolled release. This study aimed to develop and evaluate bee venom-loaded nanoliposomes (BV-LN) as an innovative Antioxidant and erythroprotective delivery platform with controlled in vitro release and enhanced gastrointestinal stability for potential applications in neurodegenerative disease management. BV’s antioxidant activity, erythroprotective potential, hemocompatibility, and…

arquivo.titulo: The anthidiine bees of Pakistan: taxonomic housekeeping with the description of a new species of Anthidium (Hymenoptera: Megachilidae: Anthidiini)
arquivo.autores: Max Kasparek, Naveed Ahmed
arquivo.resumo: Megachilid bees of the tribe Anthidiini are distributed across most zoogeographic regions of the world but are notably underrepresented in South and Southeast Asia. In Pakistan, knowledge of these bees remains limited and fragmented across the literature. In a survey of Anthidiini in Pakistan, we confirmed the presence of 17 species. At least eight more species have been reported from the country, but are excluded from our list as these records have not withstood critical evaluation. Among the confirmed species, six belong to the West Palaearctic faunal region, another six to the Indo-Malayan…

arquivo.titulo: Improving the standardization of wild bee occurrence data: Towards a formal wild bee data standard
arquivo.autores: Du Clos, Brianne
arquivo.revista: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
arquivo.resumo: Conservation and management of wild bees is hindered by the variety of ways wild bee occurrence data are recorded, managed, and shared. Here, we present solutions to address this issue and introduce The Wild Bee Data Standard, a standardized means of recording and reporting data associated with wild bee occurrences, including physical specimens and photo observations. This standard aligns with contemporary data management practices widely adopted by the broader biodiversity data community. We propose a set of terms for the standard that describe various features of bee occurrences, including…

arquivo.titulo: Positive Effects of Human Action on the Establishment of Native Stingless Bees in an Urban Environment
arquivo.autores: Heloane Rocha Nascimento, Alexandre Coletto da Silva, Alex Riul Fernandes, Gabriela Fraga Porto, Kleber Del‐Claro
arquivo.revista: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
arquivo.resumo: Facilitation is an ecological interaction in which an organism modifies the environment, benefiting other species. In urban areas, tree pruning conducted to prevent contact with electrical networks can create microhabitats, such as cavities and cut branches, that serve as nesting sites for arthropods, especially bees. arquivo.autores: Eleni Gemtou
arquivo.resumo: Urban public art increasingly operates as an aesthetic interface through which sociotechnical systems of ecological governance and public legitimacy are made visible or obscured. arquivo.resumo: Wing wear in bees (Hymenoptera: Apidae) accumulates through flight activity and can serve as a proxy for foraging effort and age, yet methods for quantifying wear rely on coarse categorical scoring or simple geometric measurements that do not capture the complexity of wing edge degradation. arquivo.resumo: Carpenter bees (Xylocopa spp.) are well known for their ability to excavate nesting galleries in woody substrates; however, the use of nonwoody materials is infrequently documented. arquivo.autores: Robert Shumake

arquivo.resumo: The Omaha Bee was a dominant force in Midwestern journalism, founded in 1871 by Edward Rosewater. arquivo.titulo: Local management at low‐ to moderate‐intensity benefits wild bees in European calcareous grasslands while landscape conservation effects vary
arquivo.autores: Ira Hannappel, Catrin Westphal, Jordi Artola, Xabier Cabodevilla, Jelle Devalez, David Giralt et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Calcareous grasslands are important habitats for many pollinators including wild bees but have declined dramatically in habitat quantity and quality due to land use changes at local and landscape scale. Such developments might be mitigated by local management, such as low‐intensity land use and landscape measures, including the conservation of calcareous grasslands and the establishment of biodiversity‐friendly farming practices like agri‐environment schemes (AES). Yet, the effectiveness of these measures for conserving pollinator communities is still poorly explored and might…

arquivo.titulo: Intensive arable farming calls for resilient wild bee restoration amid severe abundance fluctuations
arquivo.autores: Imre Sándor Piross, Áron Domonkos Bihaly, Viktor Szigeti, Ildikó Arany, Imre Demeter, Fruzsina Kőhalmi et al.
arquivo.resumo: Intensive arable farming threatens wild bees by reducing floral and nesting resources, increasing agrochemical exposure, and amplifying climatic stress. Ecological restoration using native wildflower mixtures is a promising intervention to recover pollinator diversity and the ecosystem service of pollination. However, restoration outcomes remain context dependent, and it is still poorly understood how restoration can be sustainably integrated into agricultural landscapes over time. We used a replicated, landscape-scale field experiment in East-Central Europe (Hungary) to test how spatial…

arquivo.titulo: Navigating through the high species diversity of wild bees (Hymenoptera: Apoidea) requires more than identification keys
arquivo.autores: Noé Barbier Chabot, Vincent Carlier, A. Perrard
arquivo.resumo: Abstract In the context of pollinator decline and species-focused conservation measures, the need for data on wild bees continues to grow, and identifying them at a species level has become a crucial issue. This challenge is linked to a lack of naturalist skills, to the difficulty of the group, but also to a lack of tools to train people in this expertise, such as accessible, comprehensive, and up-to-date identification keys. Online multi-access keys are designed to facilitate identification, better illustrate criteria, and enable more fluid updates. These keys require a higher initial…

arquivo.titulo: Farmers' attitudes towards biodiversity shape the effectiveness of biodiversity-friendly management practices for wild bees, but not plants and spiders
arquivo.autores: Jeroen A. Scheper, David Kleijn, Fabian Klebl, Anneli Adler, Andràs Báldí, Ígnasi Bartomeus et al.
arquivo.resumo: Biodiversity continues to decline in European agricultural landscapes despite policies that promote biodiversity-friendly farming. While the ecological drivers of the effectiveness of biodiversity-friendly practices are well-studied, less is known about how farmers' attitudes influence biodiversity outcomes. We examined, in eight European countries, whether positive farmer attitudes towards biodiversity are related to higher on-field biodiversity levels and effectiveness of biodiversity-friendly practices. We combined farmer attitude surveys with field inventories of wild plants, bees and…

arquivo.titulo: Biocultural Conservation of Wild Bees: A Review of Indigenous Knowledge Systems and Veterinary Perspectives for Wildlife Conservation (2020–2026)
arquivo.autores: Lauriane Mariamé, Elena Giannottu
arquivo.resumo: In recent years, wild bee decline has emerged as a major conservation challenge driven by interacting ecological, health-related, and socio-environmental pressures. Although Indigenous Knowledge Systems (IKS) have long documented bee ecology, environmental change, and sustainable stewardship practices, their contribution remains insufficiently integrated into contemporary conservation and veterinary frameworks. This review evaluates the current evidence on how IKS can contribute to wild bee conservation and examines how these knowledge systems can be integrated with ecological and veterinary…

arquivo.titulo: Traditional ecological knowledge about bees among Guarani and Kaiowá indigenous students in central-western Brazil: implications for pollinator conservation
arquivo.autores: Walkiria Aparecida Benites, Laura Jane Gisloti, Gislaine Monfort
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Global pollinator decline threatens biodiversity and ecosystem services, yet long-term monitoring remains scarce in much of the Neotropics. Traditional ecological knowledge (TEK) may help fill part of this gap, but TEK-based approaches remain underused in insect conservation. We examined bee-related knowledge and perceptions among 150 Guarani and Kaiowá Indigenous students enrolled at FAIND/UFGD, Dourados, Brazil, across six cohorts from 2019 to 2024. The study combined structured questionnaires, a visual recognition task, and textual similarity analysis of open-ended responses. The…

arquivo.titulo: Bumble bee abundance and diversity increase with the intensity of tallgrass prairie restoration intervention
arquivo.autores: Jade M. Kochanski, Stephanie L. McFarlane, Ellen I. Damschen, Claudio Gratton
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Introduction Human land use intensification and the resulting habitat loss are primary drivers of insect pollinator declines. Habitat restoration offers a promising approach to counteract these declines, yet landscape‐level evaluations of bee responses to restoration and management remain limited. We conducted a 2‐year, landscape‐scale study in Wisconsin, United States, to assess how different intensities of tallgrass prairie restoration and management affect bumble bees ( Bombus spp.). Objectives This study aimed to determine whether (1) bumble bee abundance and diversity increase…

arquivo.autores: Skaou A, Aglagane A, Tourbez C, Er‐Rguibi O, Benkhalifa H, Sentil A et al.
arquivo.resumo: Almond trees are economically important and widely cultivated across the Mediterranean. Their yield depends on cross‐pollination by insects, yet their pollinators remain largely unknown, particularly in North Africa. This study investigated the diversity, abundance and pollen affinity of wild bee species in a Moroccan almond orchard. Using sweep netting and pan traps, a total of 813 specimens representing 104 species, 17 genera and 5 families were recorded in the studied orchard. Bee diversity and abundance peaked during the flowering phase, reflecting the key role of bloom phenology in…

arquivo.titulo: Regional environmental filters modulate the bee community in a landscape impacted by Brazil's largest mining disaster
arquivo.autores: Kamilla Castelan, Flávio Mariano Machado Mota, Milton Barbosa, Kleber  Felipe Alves da Silva, Eduardo A. B. Almeida, Marcio L. Oliveira et al.
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT The collapse of the Fundão dam in 2015 was Brazil's most serious environmental disaster, but our understanding of its long-term effects on pollinator communities is limited by the absence of pre-disaster surveys. This reflects a gap in research on pollinators in mining affected landscapes. The Fundão dam belonged to mining company Samarco, and this study evaluated the effects of mining tailings on bee communities along the Rio Doce watershed, comparing impacted sites (IS) and reference sites (RS; non-impacted) in five regions. The bee survey yielded 10,721 individuals from 88 species…

arquivo.titulo: Effects of Native Grass Circular Buffer Strips on Native Bee Populations and Diversity in Pivot-Irrigated Corn
arquivo.autores: Michaelyne J. Wilkinson, C. Scott Bundy, Matthew Tryc, Sangamesh V. Angadi
arquivo.resumo: Native and domestic bee diversity was studied in circular buffer strips of native grasses compared with diversity in a corn monoculture in New Mexico during 2020 and 2021. The field site was composed of a monoculture of corn and an interplanting of corn with a New Mexico perennial native grass mix in buffer strips. Bee populations were sampled in each plot by using colored pan traps. A total of 8,863 bees from 5 families, identified to 24 genera, 6 tribes, and 2 subfamilies, were collected during this study. The most common bees collected were Lasioglossum spp. (Halictidae) and Perdita spp.…

arquivo.resumo: Ectoparasites are among the most significant threats to the health and survival of both managed and wild bees, yet their diversity and distribution in tropical ecosystems remain poorly documented. We surveyed ectoparasites associated with honeybees Apis mellifera and stingless bees (Meliponini) across 25 localities on Colombia’s Pacific coast (Valle del Cauca and Cauca Departments). Each sampling point comprised approximately 10–20 managed or free-living colonies, in total, 4572 specimens were collected, including 3414 A. mellifera (226 from free-living colonies, 3188 from commercial…

arquivo.titulo: Species composition, elevational distribution and morphometric analysis of bumble bees in Jammu region, J&K
arquivo.autores: Ankita Guleria, Rakesh Kumar Gupta, Marvi Khajuria, Vishrava Katoch
arquivo.resumo: The Himalayas are among the most biodiverse regions on earth, yet the distribution and abundance of many plant and animal species in this area remain poorly understood. Bumble bees, which are cold-adapted insects that thrive at high altitudes, play a crucial ecological and economic role in the pollination of wildflowers and crops. This two-year study, conducted in Jammu (J&K) examined the altitudinal distribution, morphometric characteristics, and floral associations of bumble bees across different elevations. A total of 223 specimens representing five species were collected, with maximum…

arquivo.autores: Claire Carvell, Nick J. B. Isaac, Martin C. Harvey, Robin Hutchinson, Nadine Mitschunas, Christopher Andrews et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Declines in pollinating insects are a cause for concern, yet modelling abundance trends remains challenging and most species are not covered by long‐term standardised monitoring We produce new metrics of change for insect pollinators which incorporate multi‐scale environmental variables into the modelling process to account for various sources of noise and potential bias. Data were generated from three surveys under the UK Pollinator Monitoring Scheme (PoMS) over 5‐ and 6‐year periods, measuring (i) insect abundance and species richness of bees and hoverflies from pan traps across a…

arquivo.titulo: A matter of time: Optimising bee sampling while limiting bycatch
arquivo.autores: André Krahner, Wiebke Kämper, Severin Polreich, Oleg Lewkowski
arquivo.resumo: Pan traps are an established method for sampling bees across a wide range of habitats and geographical regions, but uncertainty persists to what extent pan-trap characteristics influence sampling results. We therefore investigated how pan-trap exposure time (24 h, 48 h and 72 h) affected sampled bee communities and bycatch (insects without bees) at 23 agricultural sites in Germany, using fluorescent blue, white and yellow pan traps. We assessed abundance (number of bees), biomass of bees, total biomass, and taxon richness of bees and bycatch using DNA metabarcoding. Overall, we collected 4963…

arquivo.autores: Will Glenny, Sandra J. DeBano, Scott R. Mitchell, Mary Rowland, Zachary Hajian‐Forooshani, Skyler J. Burrows et al.
arquivo.resumo: Understanding how landscape heterogeneity promotes biodiversity remains a significant challenge because the drivers of community assembly co-vary across space and time. Contrasting ecological conditions between habitat types strengthen filters that can select for complementary communities at local scales, but it remains unclear how the seasonal variation of species assemblage within a habitat type influences overall diversity. arquivo.autores: Samuel R. Wilhelm, Laura Russo, Maya M. Lapp, Mark A. Turner, Craig A. Harper
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Introduction Native plant communities have declined in the southeastern United States over the past century because of habitat loss and fire suppression. While restoration of these communities often requires prescribed fire, the effects of fire on endemic insects remain unclear. Pollinators of savanna plants, including bees, are an important group to study in restoration contexts. Fire timing and frequency may impact both plant composition and plant‐bee interactions. arquivo.autores: Sophie Kratschmer, Samira Linhart, Peter Unglaub, Markus Milchram, Markus Immitzer, Christian Holler et al.

arquivo.autores: Jasmin Hackl, Stefan Dötterl
arquivo.resumo: Natural gardens with a high diversity of native plants, heterogeneous habitats and the absence of pesticides can serve as refuges and important secondary habitats for numerous animal species. However, little is known about the diversity of wild bees, the most important pollinators worldwide, in such natural gardens, and even less is known about the wild bee fauna of natural gardens where measures to specifically support bees have been implemented. Here, the wild bee fauna of a highly structured private natural garden in Austria of about 3700 m2, which is managed to specifically promote wild…

arquivo.autores: Mae Vaughan, Scott Black
arquivo.resumo: Excerpt: Over one hundred crop species in North America require a visit from an insect pollinator to be most productive. In the past, native bees and feral honey bees could meet the pollination needs of small orchards, tomato and pumpkin fields, and berry patches, because these farms were typically adjacent to areas of habitat that harbored important pollinators. Today, many farms are large and, at the same time, have less nearby habitat to support native pollinators. To ensure adequate pollination services, producers now rely on European honey bees. arquivo.autores: Flavio Esposito, Attena Rashidi, Federica Granata, Carmine Vitagliano, Alessio Avino, Lucia Sansone et al.
arquivo.resumo: This work presents a wavelength-encoded fiber optic interferometric platform for real-time biofilm detection and monitoring. The sensors were realized through a simple and cost-effective fabrication procedure based on overlap fusion splicing of standard single-mode optical fibers. Numerical simulations were conducted to provide design guidelines and achieve high sensitivity. The fabricated devices exhibited a sensitivity to the surrounding medium refractive index (SRI) of approximately 200 nm/RIU in aqueous solutions. The platform was first validated by monitoring Pseudomonas alcaligenes…

arquivo.resumo: Microorganisms found in stingless native bee hives have been studied for their functional potential and applicability in probiotic products and bioinputs. This review aims to compile the main scientific evidence on the microorganisms present in these symbiotic systems and discuss their applications in the food, health, and agriculture sectors. The research was conducted using PubMed and ScienceDirect databases, covering publications from 2015 to 2025. A bibliometric analysis with the VOSviewer software was used to map scientific trends and knowledge gaps. The studies analyzed reveal that…

arquivo.autores: Caio S. Ballarin, Jorge Isla, Blanca Arroyo‐Correa, Elena Quintero, Leandro Hachuy‐Filho, Felipe Wanderley Amorim et al.
arquivo.resumo: Plant-pollinator interactions are dynamic not only across seasons but also over hourly time scales, even beyond the day-night contrast. However, capturing the daily temporal variability of pollination networks during field data collection is challenging. Consequently, our understanding of daily variation in network composition and structure remains incomplete due to limited sampling coverage. Moreover, inaccurate sampling protocols can result in missing links that impair the identification of underlying processes and emerging patterns. We address this gap by studying the fine-scale temporal…

arquivo.autores: Arthur Vesaro, Fábio Eder Cardoso
arquivo.resumo: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the abelhas.org website, highlighting the importance of this resource for the conservation of stingless bee culture and revealing the lack of a specific software that fully meets the needs of stingless bee keepers. The research adopted a qualitative-quantitative approach, using questionnaires to collect data from stingless bee keepers. The results suggest a lack of government incentives, the influence of external forces that threaten the conservation of stingless bee keeping, and the presence of clandestine and enigmatic activities on the…

arquivo.resumo: Pollination is a crucial ecosystem service sustaining plant reproduction, biodiversity, and ecosystem functioning. Understanding how pollinator communities respond to environmental factors is therefore essential for supporting pollinator services, particularly in agricultural landscapes. We surveyed three pollinator taxa, wild bees, hoverflies and butterflies, across 26 semi-arid grassland sites in Vojvodina (Serbia) during three seasons in 2022. arquivo.resumo: Abstract Bees are key pollinators that support global food production and plant biodiversity, yet wild pollinator populations are declining due to anthropogenic pressures, including habitat loss, pesticide use, and emerging disease. In honey bees ( Apis mellifera ), viral disease dynamics have been strongly influenced by the parasitic mite Varroa destructor , which vectors Deformed Wing Virus (DWV) and has altered viral community composition. Predicting species distributions in agricultural regions can be challenging due to historical under-sampling in those areas and the presence of small landscape elements or non-productive land adjacent to the agricultural fields. Objectives Here we model bees and hoverflies in Dutch agricultural regions at a 10 m resolution to measure the improvement in habitat suitability predictions when landscape elements are included as model parameters. In the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster a neural circuit in the central complex of the brain serves as an internal compass, exploiting a network architecture called a ring attractor 1, 2 . arquivo.resumo: This review evaluates the role of agroecological infrastructures, including flower strips, hedgerows, grasslands, field margins, and semi-natural habitats, in supporting pollinator communities within agricultural systems. arquivo.autores: Megan A. Sampognaro, Skyler J. Burrows, Katie Moriarty, Jake P. Verschuyl, Dustin G. Gannon, James W. Rivers

In this study, we evaluated bee communities in shaded fuel breaks (n = 27) and untreated reference sites (n = 9) on private conifer forests of northern California during 2023-2024. Across both years we captured 17,124 bees comprising 5 families, 33 genera, and 188 species. arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT The breeding systems of Lutruwita/Tasmania's threatened Epacris taxa are poorly known. Our main objective was to determine the pollinators of several endemic species and explore for relationships between pollinators, floral morphology, flowering time and habitat. The Epacris have limited variation in floral traits and exhibit generalist floral visitor profiles. arquivo.resumo: Bees in the Amazon play an essential role beyond honey, pollen, and propolis production, acting as key pollinators of native flora. Understanding the floral resources used by Scaptotrigona nigrohirta supports meliponiculture, a sustainable regional activity. A melissopalynological analysis was performed on twelve honey samples to determine the botanical origin of the pollen in honey produced by this species and to support conservation strategies. arquivo.resumo: Disaster-prone areas require intelligent, real-time environmental monitoring systems to anticipate and mitigate ecological risks.This study introduces a novel optimization framework for flora-based monitoring using the Queen Honey Bee Migration (QHBM) algorithm in an Internet of Things system.This approach integrates edge computing, mobile-based image acquisition, and convolutional neural networks to emit vegetation health indicators as important proxies for predicting floods and landslides.The optimization problem is formulated as a multi-objective tradeoff involving energy efficiency,…

arquivo.key: t:forest entomofauna mediated ecosystem services in northwestern himalayan landscapes
arquivo.titulo: Forest entomofauna mediated ecosystem services in northwestern Himalayan landscapes
arquivo.autores: R. K. Gupta, Kamlesh Bali, Ranjana Bali
arquivo.resumo: Insects constitute the functional backbone of forest ecosystems through pollination, decomposition, nutrient cycling and biological control. However, information on their diversity and seasonal dynamics across Himalayan altitudinal gradients remains limited. The present study evaluated the influence of altitude and seasonality on entomofaunal diversity and abundance across three forest landscape zones of the northwestern Himalayas: lower Shiwaliks (≤1100 m asl), mid Shiwaliks (1101–1800 m asl), and Middle Himalayas (>1800 m asl). Seasonal surveys were conducted from March 2022 to December…

arquivo.titulo: Neurological sequelae of massive bee envenomation: a rare case report of watershed cerebral infarction and hemorrhage
arquivo.autores: Arati Baskota, Pujan Pokharel, Harsha Madhu, Nischal Subedi, Aswath Ramesh
arquivo.resumo: Introduction and significance: Bee stings are common but can cause severe systemic reactions, including anaphylaxis, cardiovascular instability, and, rarely, neurological complications such as watershed cerebral infarctions, as well as death. Stroke following bee envenomation is uncommon and may result from multiple pathological mechanisms. Case presentation: A 65-year-old male presented to the emergency department 30 minutes after sustaining more than 60 bee stings. He exhibited hypotension (BP 90/50 mmHg), hypoxia (SpO₂ 88%), generalized swelling, and respiratory distress. Initial…

arquivo.titulo: Communicating data quality from citizen science: lessons learned from environmental monitoring studies
arquivo.autores: Jan Brus
arquivo.resumo: The global expansion of citizen science has fundamentally transformed environmental monitoring and conservation practices.While volunteer-contributed data offers unprecedented spatial and temporal coverage, it introduces significant challenges in data quality assessment and communication.This work presents methodological approaches and lessons learned from two long-term citizen science projects focused on environmental monitoring: (1) mosquito outbreak mapping in a protected landscape area in Czechia, and (2) international monitoring of honey bee colony losses through the COLOSS network.Both…

arquivo.titulo: A comparison of the efficiency of kairomone lures for Bruchus rufimanus monitoring
arquivo.autores: ANTOINE PICHON, Sheila Alves, Eamon David Nolan, Louise McNamara
arquivo.resumo: The bruchid beetle Bruchus rufimanus Boh. is a common pest in Europe affecting grain quality of faba bean Vicia faba L. and reducing its marketability. The control of this pest in Europe mainly relies on spraying pyrethroid insecticides in the field. However, because of its biology and low sensitivity to pyrethroid the control of this pest remains challenging. New control methods need to rely on integrated pest management programs (IPM). Semiochemical traps appear as a promising IPM tool by providing monitoring information, but also by its potential use as a mass-trapping control method. In…

arquivo.titulo: Forest edges buffer effects of agricultural management on bee–plant interaction networks
arquivo.autores: Samantha Marx de Castro, Cauê Nagatani, Vânia Nobuko Yoshikawa, Franciny Yuko Urushima, Kelli dos Santos Ramos, Guaraci Duran Cordeiro et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Bee–plant interaction networks are essential for sustaining pollination services in agricultural landscapes, and farming practices can modify their structure by altering species composition and interaction patterns along crop margins. This study assessed how conventional and organic management influence bee–plant interaction networks and key network metrics (connectance, nestedness, interaction richness, interaction diversity and modularity) along crop field edges bordering native forest fragments. Surveys conducted on farms growing different crops revealed similar bee and plant…

arquivo.titulo: Nocturnal pollination services as an ecological safety net for papaya production in a tropical biodiversity hotspot
arquivo.autores: Mark Otieno, Marcell K. Peters, Sara Marie Plesser, Jie Zhang, Ingolf Steffan‐Dewenter
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Pollination is of key importance for tropical agriculture, yet a bee-centred perspective often overlooks the critical role of nocturnal insects in pollination services. We evaluated the relative contributions of diurnal and nocturnal pollinators to papaya yields on subsistence farms in the Taita Hills, Kenya, a globally important biodiversity hotspot. We combined flower visitor observations with five experimental treatments: open pollination, wind-only (closed), hand pollination, and temporal exclusions for day-only and night-only services. Our results reveal complete temporal niche…

arquivo.titulo: 3D-printed flowers for standardised pollinator monitoring
arquivo.autores: Carlos Martínez‐Núñez, Rocío Sánchez-López, Domingo Cano, Antonio Pérez, Felix Neff, Corina Maurer et al.
arquivo.resumo: Global declines in insect pollinators have triggered the need for standardised, scalable methods to monitor pollinator populations. Automated photomonitoring and machine-learning-based identification are emerging as promising non-lethal approaches for large-scale insect observation, but their effectiveness requires reliable and consistent monitoring designs. Artificial flowers offer a solution to limitations associated with natural flowers, including variability in floral availability, lack of standardisation, and wind-induced noise in visual data, yet their performance under real field…

arquivo.titulo: Alternative Livelihood Options and Forest Resources Conservation in Cross River State, Nigeria
arquivo.autores: Comfort Omari Ogbor, Comfort Nkongho Agbor
arquivo.resumo: The purpose of this study was to investigate alternative livelihood options and forest resources conservation in Cross River State. To achieve the purpose of this study, 2 null hypotheses were formulated to guide the study. Conceptual and empirical literature were reviewed in accordance with the variables of the study. Predictive correlational research design was utilized for the study. The population of the study comprised all adult residents in forest communities in Cross River State. The ten local government areas and fifty-seven communities used for the study were proportionately selected…

arquivo.titulo: Camera-trap monitoring reveals flower visitor diversity and diel activity patterns in the forest understory: bramble patches (Rubus fruticosus agg.) as a model system
arquivo.autores: Louise Bonneau-Chloup, Cécile Hignard, Baptiste Lemaire, Sophie Pasek, Sylvie Meyer, Laurence Walch
arquivo.resumo: Pollinator communities in deciduous temperate forest understories remain poorly understood, particularly regarding the relative roles of temporal activity patterns and microclimatic conditions in structuring flower visitor assemblages. We developed a non-invasive video monitoring system to investigate flower visitor communities on brambles (Rubus fruticosus agg.) across four forest patches in the Fontainebleau forest (Île-de-France, France), recording 3,636 visits from 17 morphotype groups during 369 hours. Ants dominated visits (45%), followed by non-syrphid flies (10%), whereas bees,…

arquivo.titulo: Melittological notes from Guatemala (Hymenoptera: Anthophila), 3. New country records for Halictidae (Halictini)
arquivo.autores: Ana Cristina Garcia-Cordon, Joel Gardner, José Monzón-Sierra, Richard S. Zack, Silas Bossert
arquivo.resumo: We present three new country records for sweat bees (Hymenoptera: Halictidae: Halictini) for Guatemala: Agapostemon atrocaeruleus (Friese, 1917), Lasioglossum exiguum (Smith, 1879), and L. obnubilum (Sandhouse, 1924). The records of A. atrocaeruleus and L. exiguum contribute to filling the knowledge gap of the known distribution in Mexico and Central America. The new L. obnubilum record expands the known distribution of the species further south, making it the southernmost presently known record. Additionally, we expand the known distribution within Guatemala for four Lasioglossum (Dialictus)…

arquivo.titulo: New distribution records of two Lithurgus bee species (Hymenoptera: Megachilidae) from Jammu & Kashmir, India
arquivo.autores: P.M. Osman Javid, Sajad H. Parey
arquivo.resumo: The present study provides new distributional record of Lithurgus bees of the family Megachilidae. Lithurgus albofacialis (Gupta) and Lithurgus atratus (Smith) are new records for Jammu & Kashmir region. Detailed notes on diagnostic features, material examined, and precise locality data are provided. These findings extend the known geographical range of both species in the region and contribute to the understanding of Megachilidae diversity in India. The study underscores the importance of continued faunal surveys for documenting the bee fauna of the Himalayan biodiversity hotspot.

arquivo.titulo: Multiple bee stings leading to a delayed fatal coronary event with probable Kounis syndrome: a case report
arquivo.autores: Mallapu Ajay Kumar, Poonam Arora, BharatBhushan Bhardwaj, Parina Tejpal, Pavan Anjaiah, Jyoti Chauhan et al.
arquivo.resumo: BACKGROUND: Kounis syndrome-an acute coronary syndrome occurring in the setting of allergic or hypersensitivity reactions-remains an under-recognised clinical entity. In many cases, the diagnosis is largely probabilistic, particularly in the absence of confirmatory evidence such as mast-cell activation markers or intracoronary imaging. In the present context, while the clinical history of bee sting strongly supports Kounis syndrome as the most likely differential diagnosis, definitive confirmation is limited by the lack of objective mast-cell-related investigations. We report a 72-year-old…

arquivo.titulo: Entre la conservación y la producción: polinizadores silvestres y sus servicios en agroecosistemas de Chile
arquivo.autores: Alejandra E. Muñoz
arquivo.resumo: Biotic pollination is a key ecosystem service that supports both biodiversity conservation and agricultural production. However, its provision is increasingly threatened by agricultural intensification, and other environmental pressures. In Chile, this issue is particularly relevant because most agricultural activity occurs within a global biodiversity hotspot characterized by exceptionally high levels of endemism, including one of the world’s major hotspots for bee diversity. This article reviews current knowledge on wild pollinators and the pollination services they provide in Chilean…

arquivo.titulo: Towards Acoustic Bioindicator Integration in AI-Based Wildfire Monitoring: A Systematic Review
arquivo.autores: Mustafa S, Mohaghegh M, Ardekani I, Sarrafzadeh A
arquivo.resumo: Wildfires are becoming more frequent, severe, and long-lasting, driving rapid growth in sensor-based and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled systems for early detection and risk assessment. This article presents a systematic literature review, based on 169 studies screened from 7511 records, of wildfire monitoring approaches using satellite and aerial remote sensing, fixed cameras, wireless sensor networks, and Internet of Things (IoT) platforms combined with machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models for ignition detection, fire-weather indices, spread prediction, and burned-area…

arquivo.titulo: First record of gynandromorphy in Andrena florivaga and an additional case in Nomada lathburiana from Germany (Hymenoptera, Apoidea)
arquivo.autores: Marcel Kettermann, Juliana Klaren, Christina Rupprecht, Christoph Bleidorn, Thomas Fartmann
arquivo.resumo: Rare developmental anomalies can provide valuable insights into the mechanisms of sex differentiation, particularly when they manifest in clearly defined morphological patterns. In this study, we describe the first recorded gynandromorph of Andrena florivaga and a further gynandromorphic specimen of Nomada lathburiana from Germany. The Andrena florivaga specimen shows a predominantly bilateral display of sexually dimorphic traits, with male structures largely restricted to one side of the body while female traits dominate the opposite side; the head and forelegs represent entirely the female…

arquivo.titulo: Distributed PV Hosting Capacity Enhancement Under Extreme High-Temperature Conditions Using an Improved Multi-Objective Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm
arquivo.autores: Aimin Wang, Yiqiong Wang, Ruizhe Jia, Jiye Liang
arquivo.resumo: The frequent occurrence of extreme high-temperature events has significantly affected the operating characteristics and distributed photovoltaic (PV) hosting capacity of distribution networks. However, existing hosting capacity assessment methods rarely consider the accumulated heat effect caused by sustained high temperatures. To address this issue, this paper proposes a coordinated planning method for enhancing distributed PV hosting capacity under extreme high-temperature scenarios. First, an accumulated heat load model is developed to characterize the temporal cumulative influence of…

arquivo.titulo: Avian Diversity in Agroforestry Landscapes of Kolar District of Karnataka A Rapid Farmer’s Field Survey Assessment Outcomes
arquivo.autores: Jay Anand, Harshavardhana- Hari Prasad, Kevin Johnal, Praveen Raj, Jarun Simson, Dinesh Babu et al.
arquivo.revista: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
arquivo.resumo: Agroforestry is increasingly recognised as a land-use system capable of reconciling agricultural production with biodiversity conservation, yet quantitative information on avian diversity in farmer-managed agroforestry landscapes remains scarce in semi-arid India. This paper reports a rapid assessment of avian diversity in farmer-managed agroforestry plots in Kolar district, Karnataka, undertaken between January and July 2026 as an adjunct to farmer-on boarding surveys for an Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR) carbon project. Birds were recorded opportunistically (ad libitum)…

arquivo.titulo: The Genome Exposome Microbiome–Phenome (GEM–P): a conceptual framework for social bees
arquivo.autores: Simone Cutajar, Daniele Alberoni, Diana Di Gioia, David Mifsud
arquivo.resumo: Abstract The gut microbiome of social bees is a small, specific set of symbionts that contributes to nutrition, detoxification, immune function and behaviour, with effects on colony performance and resilience. In recent years, the field has expanded, but studies still analyse host genetics and environmental exposures separately and often rely on correlations between microbes and health traits. This makes it difficult to distinguish between instances in which microbiome differences primarily reflect host or environmental factors and instances in which they may contribute mechanistically to bee…

arquivo.titulo: A State-Sensing Adaptive Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm with Dynamic Search and Rank-Based Selection for High-Dimensional Complex Optimization
arquivo.autores: Xinyao Gao
arquivo.resumo: Abstract  Standard Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) suffers from poor initialization, imbalanced exploration and exploitation in its one-dimensional search mechanism, and weakening selection pressure, limiting convergence speed, accuracy, and stability. This paper proposes State-Sensing Adaptive ABC (SSA-ABC). It senses the problem's dimensionality and uses sigmoid dynamic hybrid initialization combining Latin hypercube sampling, random initialization, and a reflection-hybrid boundary mechanism. It senses progress via function evaluation ratio to dynamically adjust search from one-dimensional…

arquivo.titulo: Comparing ecological and economic benefits of organic farming and annual flower strips
arquivo.autores: Péter Batáry, Costanza Geppert, Rita Földesi, Róbert Gallé, Katalin Szitár, Edina Török et al.
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Across the EU, common agri‐environment schemes (AES) comprise measures such as organic farming, which prohibits synthetic agrochemicals, and wildflower strips. We evaluated the ecological and economic effectiveness of non‐productive annual wildflower strips adjacent to conventional wheat fields and productive organic wheat fields. Our study spanned nine landscapes, each containing three types of winter wheat fields: conventional with a wildflower strip, conventional without strip as a control (no AES) and organic field. Over 2 years, we surveyed plants and sampled carabids, spiders…

arquivo.titulo: Harnessing Amazonian biodiversity for sustainable and circular food systems
arquivo.autores: José M. Álvarez-Suárez, Henrik Balslev
arquivo.resumo: The Amazon Basin’s underused biodiversity can transform fragile food systems into resilient and circular ones. This Perspective explores how Amazonian biodiversity could serve as a foundation for sustainable food-system transitions through circular bioeconomy strategies, biodiversity-based food innovations, and inclusive governance models. Fruits, oilseeds, insects, and stingless bee honeys provide essential nutrients and bioactive compounds while supporting circular value chains with potential to reduce post-harvest losses, restore ecosystems, and diversify diets. Realising this potential…

arquivo.titulo: Enterotype signatures of multi-stressor exposure inform conservation strategies for mountain bumblebees of the subgenus Pyrobombus
arquivo.autores: Xin Xu, Ruiqing Cao, Jiu-Hong Dong, Zong‐Xin Ren, Yanhui Zhao, Huanhuan Zhu et al.
arquivo.resumo: Bees often exhibit gut microbiome-defined enterotypes impacting their health and pollination services. Bumblebees, keystone pollinators in montane and agriculture ecosystems, face significant population declines might linked to gut parasites, pathogens, and antibiotic exposure; however, whether their enterotypes reflect these specific stressors remains uncharacterized. Here, we investigate the gut microbiomes of two bumblebee species belonging to the subgenus Pyrobombus, which are commonly infested by the gut parasite Crithidia bombi and other pathogens with samples over four years in…

arquivo.titulo: Disappearing Natives, Emerging Invasives: Indigenous Knowledge, Biodiversity Loss, and Climate Resilience in Gandaki Province, Nepal
arquivo.autores: Myrle Ballard, Ranjan Kumar Datta, Som Prasad Niroula, Jebunnessa Chapola
arquivo.resumo: Climate change, deforestation, and chemical-intensive agriculture are rapidly reshaping ecosystems across the Global South, with profound consequences for Indigenous communities. Yet dominant biodiversity and invasive species research often marginalizes Indigenous interpretations and lived experience. This study examines how Gurung Indigenous and Dalit communities in Gandaki Province, Nepal understand shifts in native and invasive species and how these changes affect ecological balance, food security, cultural life, and climate resilience. Using community conversations and Indigenous Elder…

arquivo.titulo: Awareness and Buying Behaviour Towards BEE Star-Labelled White Goods among Working Women with Special Reference to Ramanathapuram District
arquivo.autores: S.Fathima Rustha, A. Jasmine
arquivo.revista: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
arquivo.resumo: Abstract: The increasing concern for energy conservation and environmental sustainability has enhanced consumer interest in energy-efficient household appliances. The present study examines awareness and buying behaviour towards BEE star-labelled white goods among working women with special reference to Ramanathapuram District. The study adopts a descriptive and analytical research design, with primary data collected from 385 working women through a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale. The mean score analysis indicates a high level of awareness, with an overall mean score…
