arquivo.resumo: Penerapan algoritma optimasi untuk menentukan rute terpendek merupakan salah satu cara yang efektif untuk meningkatkan efisiensi operasional dalam berbagai bidang, termasuk dalam monitoring wajib pajak. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengimplementasikan dua algoritma metaheuristik, yaitu Algoritma Semut (Ant Colony Optimization - ACO) dan Algoritma Lebah (Bee Algorithm), dalam menemukan rute terpendek bagi petugas pajak yang harus mengunjungi beberapa titik lokasi wajib pajak. Pada penelitian ini, kedua algoritma diujikan pada dataset yang berisi lokasi wajib pajak yang perlu dipantau, dengan…

arquivo.titulo: Not all crickets are equal: selective shrike predation highlights the conservation value of diverse arthropod communities to grassland birds
arquivo.autores: Leonardo Ancillotto, Sauro Giannerini, Matteo Bianchi, Giulia Santalmasi, Marco Zaccaroni, Tommaso Lipparelli et al.
arquivo.resumo: Understanding dietary preferences and prey selection is pivotal for interpreting the ecology and conservation needs of threatened species. We investigated the diet composition and prey selection of the Red‐backed Shrike Lanius collurio in a montane grassland of the central Italian Apennines, with special regard to sex‐related differences and the relationships between prey use and local prey availability. Using a non‐invasive camera‐trapping protocol at artificial perches, we collected high‐resolution photographic records of predation events over three breeding seasons (2021–2023). This method…

arquivo.key: t:bee assemblage patterns during various seasons in punjab a north western state of india
arquivo.titulo: Bee assemblage patterns during various seasons in Punjab, a north-western state of India
arquivo.autores: M. Kaur, A. Choudhary, B. Mohindru, J.R. Singh
arquivo.resumo: Bees are important pollinators necessary for both managed agroecosystems and wild landscapes. Their assemblage was measured in terms of diversity and abundance during five different seasons in Punjab, India. Random sampling was done at various locations by swaying a hand insect net 30 times over the blooms. A total of 7482 bees’ specimens were collected and identified. Among honey bees, Apis mellifera was the most abundant (12.58%), followed by Apis dorsata (12.24%), while Apis florea was the least abundant (9.18%). The seasons differ significantly with respect to the bee species. Their…

arquivo.titulo: Revision of the Italian Lasioglossum Curtis, 1833 (Hymenoptera: Halictidae), with an illustrated identification key
arquivo.autores: Simone Flaminio, Marino Quaranta, Natasha De Manincor, Denis Michez
arquivo.resumo: The genus Lasioglossum Curtis, 1833 is the most diverse group of halictid bees and is widely distributed across the Palaearctic region. In the Mediterranean Basin, a recognized biodiversity hotspot, Lasioglossum is especially well represented, yet its taxonomy remains complex and often unresolved. This is particularly true in Italy, where the fauna of the Western part of the Mediterranean Basin is mixing with the Eastern part. Moreover, previous taxonomic studies on the species recorded in Italy are sporadic, scattered across different sources, and often published in languages other than…

arquivo.titulo: Vespidae Diversity and Seasonality in Apple and Peach Orchards of North Georgia, USA
arquivo.autores: Zahra Khan, Sabrina A. Elgar, Kenneth W. McCravy, Brett R. Blaauw
arquivo.resumo: Georgia produces a variety of fruits including both peaches and apples at considerable economic value while supporting abundant insect biodiversity. Although pollinator research in southeastern orchards has primarily emphasized bees, the roles of wasps (Hymenoptera: Vespidae) remain poorly studied despite their potential as predators, pollinators, bioindicators, and management concerns. We surveyed vespid communities in adjacent apple and peach orchards at 3 commercial farm sites in northern Georgia from 2023–2025 using Malaise traps across spring, summer, and fall sampling periods. A total…

arquivo.titulo: The The Effect of Using a Roblox-Based Spelling Bee Game on Students’ Writing Achievement at SMPN 1 Tanjungpinang
arquivo.autores: Nurfadilah, Rahma Nuzulia, Satria Agust
arquivo.resumo: This study investigates the effect of using a Roblox-Based Spelling Bee Game on the writing achievement of ninth-grade students at SMPN 1 Tanjungpinang. The study is motivated by students’ difficulties in spelling English words accurately, which affects vocabulary use and clarity in narrative writing. This research employed a quantitative pre-experimental method with a one-group pre-test and post-test design. The participants were 43 ninth-grade students selected through total sampling. Data were collected through narrative writing tests administered before and after two treatment sessions…

arquivo.titulo: Enzymatic biomarkers reveal sublethal effects of thiamethoxam and fipronil on the stingless bee Melipona scutellaris
arquivo.autores: Lucas Miotelo, Jéssica Freitas Araújo, Osmar Malaspina, Roberta Cornélio Ferreira Nocelli
arquivo.revista: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part C Toxicology & Pharmacology
arquivo.resumo: Bees are key pollinators in natural and agricultural ecosystems, yet they are increasingly affected by the intensive use of pesticides. Although not primary targets of these compounds, bees may be exposed during foraging activities. Thiamethoxam and fipronil are widely used insecticides and have been implicated in pollinator decline. Stingless bees are essential pollinators in Neotropics, making the assessment of pesticide effects on these species particularly important. This study evaluated the sublethal effects of thiamethoxam and fipronil on neural and detoxification-related enzymes in the…

arquivo.titulo: Bee pollen as functional food and environmental bioindicator: current evidence and future challenges
arquivo.autores: Luigi Parrotta, Stefano Del Duca
arquivo.revista: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
arquivo.resumo: Bee pollen (BP), a plant-derived product collected by honey bees, is increasingly promoted as a functional food due to its content of proteins, essential amino acids, lipids, vitamins, minerals, and bioactive compounds such as polyphenols and flavonoids. These components underpin its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and immunomodulatory properties. This review outlines the nutritional and nutraceutical features of BP while also addressing environmental influences, safety issues, and allergenic potential. However, BP composition is highly variable, depending on botanical origin,…

arquivo.titulo: Hive position matters: spatial layout and hive colour impact forager traffic and drifting in Melipona quadrifasciata bees
arquivo.autores: Ana Paula Cipriano, Cristiano Menezes, Milly Munro, Emily Bell, Christoph Grüter
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Stingless bees are key pollinators of native and cultivated plants, and their management mostly for honey and hive commercialisation has become an increasingly popular practice in Brazil. Hives are commonly kept close together and visually similar in meliponaries, a practice that favours drifting, i.e., the return of foragers to a foreign nest. Distance between hives and layout have been identified as drivers of drifting in the Western honeybee, but evidence for stingless bees, the largest group of social bees, remains scarce. Additionally, stingless beekeepers frequently associate…

arquivo.titulo: Stingless bee honeys: the missing piece in harmonized authenticity and quality standards
arquivo.autores: José M. Álvarez-Suárez, Patricia Vit
arquivo.resumo: Stingless bee honeys are among the most chemically diverse and bioactive honeys yet remain largely excluded from international authenticity standards centered on Apis mellifera . This exclusion may limit equitable market participation and the sustainable valorization of indigenous and culturally embedded meliponiculture systems in tropical regions. We propose a harmonized framework integrating standardized sampling, multi-omic markers, functional authenticity, and inclusive governance.

arquivo.titulo: Smart Sensor-Based Hive Monitoring System Using IoT: A Distributed Architecture for Real-Time Beehive Health Assessment
arquivo.autores: Aditya Sehravat Aditya Sehravat
arquivo.revista: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
arquivo.resumo: Traditional beekeeping relies on periodic manual hive inspections, which are labor-intensive, disruptive to colonies, and unable to detect sudden changes between visits.This paper presents a low-cost, IoT-based Smart Sensor-Based Hive Monitoring System for continuous, non-invasive monitoring of honeybee colony health.The system uses three independent ESP32 nodes: a BME280 sensor for temperature, humidity, and atmospheric pressure; an INMP441 MEMS microphone for acoustic activity using on-device RMS computation; and an HX711 amplifier with a load cell for hive weight measurement.Sensor data…

arquivo.titulo: Scaling Laws Reveal a Unified Species‐Energy Relationship for Mountain Biodiversity
arquivo.autores: Zihan Jiang, Hongyan Liu, Zhiyao Tang, Jonathan M. Chase, Alexandre Antonelli, Michael Kessler et al.
arquivo.resumo: ABSTRACT Aim Energy availability is often assumed to be a primary driver of variation in biodiversity across large‐scale environmental gradients such as elevation, but support for the role of energetic constraints is far from universal. Here, we assume that these variations in energy–richness relationships might arise from the degree of match between the scale of the response of organisms to energy (response scale) and the scale of the observation made (observation scale). Location 41 mountain ecosystems worldwide, with detailed case studies on Dongling Mountain, China. Time Period…

arquivo.titulo: Pesticide Dissipation in Agroecosystems – Exploring Pesticide Fate and Transport Mechanisms to Protect Alternative Pollinators
arquivo.autores: Calvin Luu
arquivo.resumo: Honey bees are the most well-known pollinators, but there exists thousands of other bee species that contribute to pollination; one such group of bees are the solitary bees. True to their namesake, solitary bees do not live in hives like honey bees. Some solitary bees, like alfalfa leafcutting bees (ALCB) and blue orchard bees, can pollinate crops more efficiently than honey bees. However, since they live solitary lives, pesticide exposure is much more harmful to their overall population. If one honey bee dies from pesticide exposure, the hive can still survive, and the queen bee will…

arquivo.titulo: Analysis of neonicotinoid pesticides and their metabolites by liquid chromatography–electrospray ionization–tandem mass spectrometry
arquivo.autores: Andreas F. Lehner, Julia Dickie, Justin Zyskowski, John Buchweitz
arquivo.resumo: Neonicotinoid insecticides were first introduced in the 1990s as an alternative to older, more toxic types such as organophosphates, carbamates, and chlorinated hydrocarbons and have since become the most widely used class of insecticides globally. arquivo.resumo: Apiculture, or scientific beekeeping, is increasingly recognized as a multifunctional livelihood activity that integrates income generation, agricultural productivity, food security and ecosystem conservation. Unlike many agricultural enterprises, beekeeping requires relatively limited land and water resources and can be incorporated into existing farming systems. Honey, beeswax, propolis, royal jelly and other bee products provide opportunities for household income diversification, while bee-mediated pollination contributes to crop yield, quality and biodiversity. arquivo.titulo: Unequal pollinator benefits from partial mowing regimes in a field experiment
arquivo.autores: Constant Swinkels, Ilona de Weert, Paolo Biella, Eelke Jongejans, Hans de Kroon
arquivo.resumo: Abstract Studies suggest that partial mowing, where unmown refuges are left for insects after mowing, promotes arthropods in semi‐natural grasslands. However, studies comparing community development in refuges to unmown controls are scarce, particularly for insect pollinators. As competition for floral resources is a central driver in pollinator community composition, the potential increase in pollinator density within unmown refuges is likely to filter ecological communities. We here present a partial mowing field experiment on dike grasslands to study how pollinator communities develop in…

Termorregulação, tolerância térmica e cl.resumo: Bees are subject to numerous pressures in the modern world. Climate change is likely to exacerbate these problems in the future. Termorregulação, tolerância térmica e cl.resumo: Bees are major pollinators of Angiosperms and therefore their apparent decline is of importance for humans and biodiversity. We synthesise results of 12 recent reviews to provide a global picture of the threats they face. Habitat loss is the major threat to bee diversity, whilst invasive species, emerging diseases, pesticide use, and climate change also have the potential to impact bee populations. Termorregulação, tolerância térmica e cl.resumo: Bees are important pollinators of wild and agricultural plants 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 and there is increasing evidence that many bee populations decline due to a combination of habitat loss, climate change, pesticides, and other anthropogenic effects. 6 , 7 , 8 , 9 , 10 , 11 One trait that shapes both their role in plant reproduction 12 , 13 and their exposure to anthropogenic stressors is the distance at which bees forage. It has been suggested that bee sociality 14 and diet 15 affect bee foraging ranges, but how these traits and their potential interactions drive foraging ranges remains unclear.

Forrageamento e recursos florais.resumo: Euglossine bees may return to a nest from as far away as 23 kilometers in a tropical rain forest. These bees apparently forage long distances and visit the same plants repeatedly along a feeding route. They probably promote outcrossing among tropical plants with low population density; therefore, they may permit the existence of plant species whose densities have been forced very low by such things as competition and predators on seeds and seedlings.

Filogenia, sistemática e biogeografia.resumo: The stingless bee fauna currently living in Brazil is presented, including geographic records. A total of 242 species described with valid names and about 85 of new ones, affiliated to 29 genera, are registered to the country. The survey is based mainly on the Catalogue of Bees (Moure’s bee Catalogue) and specimens housed in the Camargo Collection – RPSP. An evaluation of the current taxonomic situation and some short comments about the biology of each genus are also included.

Polinização e agroecossistemas.resumo: Bees are subject to numerous pressures in the modern world. The abundance and diversity of flowers has declined; bees are chronically exposed to cocktails of agrochemicals, and they are simultaneously exposed to novel parasites accidentally spread by humans. We assessed the global exposure of pollinators to neonicotinoids by analyzing 198 honey samples from across the world.
